findings.title: Caller-owned dates can alter checked state and falsely approve an SSKR backup
findings.evidence: core-invariants.log: date ownership, pattern expansion and first-progress sentinel; sskr-boundaries.log: actual production WASM and mismatching recovered mnemonic.
findings.reproduction: Mask public abandon ... about at 23-09-2026, split 2-of-3, construct ShareBackupCheck with a retained date object and confirm restores. Change that object to day 24; checking the same shares with 24-09-2026 still reports restores although actual recovery produces a different phrase. Separately retain a DatesAnswer pattern and expand its arrays after construction: existing DateSearch grows from 365 to the 10,000,001 hard-limit sentinel and starts work. The harness stops at first progress, not a giant search.
findings.expected: Objects own an immutable validated snapshot; backup approval corresponds to actual reconstruction and searches cannot exceed validated limits through caller mutation.
findings.observed: Outer arrays are copied or frozen but nested dates/pattern arrays alias caller data. ShareBackupCheck caches held material before mutation and later compares changed dates without final recovered-phrase comparison.
findings.impact: Supported library callers can receive false backup assurance or start work beyond the checked limit. No current CLI false-pass, remote exploit, secret theft or giant search was demonstrated. EncodedBackupCheck baseline dates mutate too, but its full check has a recovered-result comparison; do not extrapolate the SSKR false-pass to it.
findings.recommendedFix: Deep-copy and freeze date/pattern graphs at ownership boundaries, return independent immutable values, and retain the validated snapshot throughout search and backup checking.
findings.requiredVerification: Retained input and getter mutation cannot change state; original-date SSKR backup restores and wrong-date backup fails; compare actual recovery; attempted post-construction limit expansion cannot start work.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: False approval of a backup contradicts a core recovery guarantee; resolve before publishing the new library API.

findings.title: DatesAnswer.of accepts invalid calendars and empty search patterns
findings.evidence: core-invariants.log: missing expected exceptions for calendar and empty pattern.
findings.reproduction: DatesAnswer.of accepts {year:2026,month:2,day:31}; it also accepts a pattern with years:[], months:[1], days:[1]. Equivalent parsed input rejects these cases.
findings.expected: The typed public constructor preserves the documented searchable invariant and validation equivalent to parsing.
findings.observed: Only outer nonemptiness and work limits are checked; invalid complete dates and zero-candidate patterns become constructed objects.
findings.impact: Bounded exported-library contract failure. Invalid calendars generally fail later in normalization; empty patterns yield no work/no matches. CLI string parsing is not shown affected; no wrong wallet result is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate calendar dates and nonempty valid candidate sets before constructing DatesAnswer; share validation with parsing.
findings.requiredVerification: Negative constructor tests for invalid calendars and empty patterns, plus valid leap-day and ordinary pattern acceptance.

findings.title: EncodedBackup.of accepts sparse index arrays
findings.evidence: core-invariants.log: missing expected exception for new Array<number>(12).
findings.reproduction: EncodedBackup.of(new Array<number>(12), 'indexes', 'direct') succeeds; unchecked seedshift-legacy has the same validation shape.
findings.expected: Every index is a present integer within the BIP39 index range before the object is constructed.
findings.observed: Array.some skips holes; constructor spread materializes undefined elements. Decoding later rejects the invalid indexes.
findings.impact: Malformed native/browser host input produces an invalid public object. CLI read creates dense arrays; no accepted incorrect mnemonic or secrecy compromise is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate every indexed position including holes, using the explicit density checks already present in candidate handling.
findings.requiredVerification: Reject sparse/partially sparse arrays, undefined and out-of-range entries; retain dense valid round-trips in all supported modes.

remediation.evidence: Owned frozen copies of dates and patterns (core/dates.ts ownedDate/ownedPattern) in DatesAnswer, DateSearch, EncodedBackupCheck and ShareBackupCheck; ShareBackupCheck.compareDates confirms the actual recovery; limits checked in the DatesAnswer constructor; patterns sharing a key with other dates and duplicate pattern values refused; ShareBackupCheck refuses modes shares are not made in. test/aud-009-remediation.test.ts; sskr-boundaries.mjs 4/4 including the retained-date SSKR reproduction; core-invariants.ts 10/12, the two pattern-mutation checks now throw TypeError because the arrays are frozen (intended). Source fingerprint 837d75eec85234a0072f48c0e37840adce151b485df15f6bb1921336fd700dbe; not committed yet.

DatesAnswer.of checks each date and pattern as parse does and names its place (Date N: ...); impossible calendar dates, empty or impossible patterns refused; leap day and ordinary patterns accepted. test/aud-009-remediation.test.ts; core-invariants.ts checks passed. Source fingerprint 837d75eec85234a0072f48c0e37840adce151b485df15f6bb1921336fd700dbe; not committed yet.

EncodedBackup checks every position in its constructor (copy first, then check), so holes, undefined and out-of-range indexes are refused through of and the raw constructor alike; the same hole check in seedshift.ts, colors.ts, candidate-list.ts and DateSearch. test/aud-009-remediation.test.ts; core-invariants.ts check passed. Source fingerprint 837d75eec85234a0072f48c0e37840adce151b485df15f6bb1921336fd700dbe; not committed yet.

recommendations: Retain real deep ownership rather than adding classes around shared mutable graphs.
Renderer global platform is a documented remaining composition limitation, not a newly hidden defect.
Optionally bind release attestation verification to expected workflow and tag commit rather than repository-only acceptance; live attestation was not verified.
conformance: ShareSet independently copies and freezes its nested graph; probe passed.
JointRepair uses the injected SharePlatform even if global configured services throw; probe passed.
All 253 newly emitted compiler files match existing dist byte-for-byte; seven SSKR integrity entries and 26 subpath exports validate.
The modular split and host-neutral public classes improve reuse; class presence alone is not correctness or runtime-speed evidence. No speed benchmark against the previous release was performed.

results.cards: 25case PDFs,5additional A6 layout checks,3member pages; raster QR checks passed

assessment: Three confirmed open findings: one medium and two low; no high/critical issue demonstrated. FUN001 blocks acceptance of the new recovery API until fixed and verified. Architecture moves in the right direction; no measured speed advantage over the previous release is established. Browser integration and release reproducibility remain unexecuted, so this is not release approval.
